clue.text: See, beer can be so rough (6)

blocks.note: beer is brewed with hops, so it can be hoppy

explanation.surface: A drinker agrees that some beer is harsh on the palate.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes "See" look like 'you see'; it is the letter C, as in texting. "beer can be so" is a description whose answer is HOPPY.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: water broken into short, rough waves is described this way.

clue.text: Lobby group agree to abandon Left (8)

indicators.note: ALIGN abandons its L, the letter standing for Left

explanation.surface: A pressure group decides to cut ties with the political left.
explanation.walkthrough: "Lobby group" reads as one noun, but "Lobby" alone is the verb definition and "group" starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to press for a cause or change.

clue.text: Sixties fad seen in old piece (2,3)

blocks.note: a piece of something is a part

explanation.surface: A 1960s craze turns up in an antique object.
explanation.walkthrough: "seen in" suggests a hidden word, but it only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art, abstract art built on optical illusions, was a craze of the 1960s.

clue.text: Cautious papa with dirty books (7)

explanation.surface: A father keeps a careful stash of smutty reading.
explanation.walkthrough: "books" is the New Testament, NT, a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone who avoids risks.

clue.text: Expert I snapped outside hotel bar (8)

indicators.note: 'outside' puts the first pieces on either side of the next, like walls around a room

blocks.note: I + BIT (snapped, as a dog does)

explanation.surface: A professional admits biting someone outside a hotel bar.
explanation.walkthrough: "hotel bar" reads as a place to drink; "bar" is the verb definition, and "snapped" is what a biting dog did.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to forbid or exclude.

clue.text: Typical but, strangely, it never repeats (14)

explanation.surface: Something is normal yet oddly never happens twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets "Typical" against "never repeats" as a paradox; the fourteen letters of "it never repeats" are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sample standing for its whole kind is typical of it.

clue.text: He plans to produce a book (7)

blocks.note: someone brewing trouble is plotting it

explanation.surface: An author sets out his plan for writing a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The book is not one he writes but one of the Bible: Hebrews, the New Testament epistle.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Epistle to the Hebrews is one book of the New Testament.

clue.text: Deformed bird egg in part of garden (9)

indicators.note: 'in' places one thing within another, as a seed sits in a bed

explanation.surface: A misshapen bird's egg is found in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: "Deformed bird egg" reads as one misshapen egg; "Deformed" is the definition and "bird egg" gives OWL EGG.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowlegged legs curve outward, a physical deformity.

clue.text: Ask for address (4,2)

blocks.note: to seek help from a friend or an expert
a verb here: to deal with a task or problem

explanation.surface: Someone requests a postal address.
explanation.walkthrough: "Ask for address" looks like one request; it splits into two definitions, with "address" as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: You turn to someone for help, and turn to a problem to deal with it.

clue.text: Train for meteorology here? (7,7)

blocks.note: the surface means study to be a forecaster; the setter means trains, as at a railway stop
asks for the place where such trains would stop

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether this is where weather forecasters study.
explanation.walkthrough: "Train" seems to mean study, but a station is where trains stop; a weather station is where weather is recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather station gathers data for meteorology, and trains stop at stations.

clue.text: Prepare to cut cloth, perhaps, and cut it (7,2)

blocks.note: a tailor measures up before cutting
to cut it is to be good enough

explanation.surface: A tailor gets ready to cut fabric, then does it.
explanation.walkthrough: "cut it" looks like the tailor's next step; it is the idiom meaning to be up to standard.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor measures up before cutting; to measure up is to cut it, being good enough.

clue.text: One inclined to make a retreat (5)

blocks.note: one who bows inclines the head

explanation.surface: Someone feels like withdrawing from the world.
explanation.walkthrough: "inclined" suggests willingness, but here it means bent over: a bower is one who bows.
explanation.definitionFit: A bower is one who bows, and also a leafy shelter to retreat to.

clue.text: Most bohemian gatherings won’t start on time (7)

indicators.note: a word that won’t start loses its first letter

blocks.note: T for time, placed on (after) ARTIES

explanation.surface: The most free-spirited parties never begin punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: Arty means affecting an artistic, bohemian style, so the superlative is ARTIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty means showily artistic, the bohemian look, so its superlative matches 'most bohemian'.

clue.text: Ultimate challenge the day before a holiday (7)

explanation.surface: A last-minute test lands just before the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: "Everest" is used figuratively for the greatest challenge anyone could face.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's highest mountain stands, figuratively, for the greatest feat anyone could attempt.

clue.text: Becomes wise, full of ideas, says Roger? (4,3,7)

indicators.note: GETS SAGE is full of THEMES

explanation.surface: Roger is said to grow wise and brim with thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: "Becomes wise" looks like the definition, but it is wordplay; "Roger" is radio talk for 'message received'.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio operator who says 'Roger' is confirming they got the message.

clue.text: Line up for a thrilling walk (9)

definitions.text: Line up for a thrilling walk

blocks.note: the surface means queue; the setter means a line (rope) strung up high
what a circus performer does along that rope

explanation.surface: People queue for an exciting stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: "Line up" reads as queue; it is a line (rope) hung up in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightrope is a line strung up high for a daring walk.

clue.text: One drunk on one cold type of drink (8)

explanation.surface: One tipsy person orders a chilled drink.
explanation.walkthrough: "drunk" is the noun, a sot, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: sports drinks matching the body's salt balance are sold under this label.

clue.text: A godsend that is somehow causing upset? (7,3,4)

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how a blessing could be distressing.
explanation.walkthrough: "upset" suggests distress; in sport an upset is a surprise win, one achieved against the odds.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport an upset is a surprise result, one achieved when the bookmakers said it would not happen.

clue.text: Pouring liquid in a circle (2-5)

indicators.note: a liquid thing flows into a new shape

explanation.surface: Liquid is poured round in a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: "liquid" seems to be what is poured, but it is the indicator acting on "Pouring".
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a clique or exclusive set of people is a circle.

clue.text: Broadcast work by author turned up in shops (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the letters read upward

blocks.note: the author of a clue refers to themselves as ME

explanation.surface: A radio version of a writer's book appears in stores.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is the author, so "author" gives ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia is a plural of emporium, a large shop.

clue.text: Plain juice? Plan rejected (6)

indicators.note: sent back, so read in reverse

explanation.surface: An unadorned drink is proposed, then turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: "Plain juice" reads as one phrase; "Plain" is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas is the vast grassy plain of South America.

clue.text: One island against another, almost (7)

indicators.note: GUAM stops short of its last letter

blocks.note: GUAM, another island, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: One island faces off against a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: Guam, the Pacific island, supplies the second island hidden in "another".
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is one of the Leeward Islands in the Caribbean.

clue.text: History will accept Sunak as supporter of shipping (7)

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the first piece takes the second inside it

blocks.note: Rishi Sunak was UK Prime Minister

explanation.surface: History will judge Rishi Sunak a friend of the shipping industry.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishi Sunak was the UK Prime Minister, hence PM; TOAST as 'done for' matches 'history'.
explanation.definitionFit: A topmast is the upper mast of a ship, holding up sails.

clue.text: Be abducted by one? (5)

indicators.note: someone abducted is carried off in the abductor's grip, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: to lie is to be or exist, as in 'the fault lies there'

explanation.surface: Someone is warned they might be carried off by a UFO visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: you might be abducted by an alien.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliens are who people claim abducted them.

clue.text: River banks needing water still (5)

indicators.note: PO lines both sides of HOT, like a river's banks

explanation.surface: A river's banks still need water.
explanation.walkthrough: "still" looks like an adverb; it is a noun, a single frame from a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a single photograph, especially one taken from or for a film.

clue.text: The opposite of “in kind” (9)

explanation.surface: Someone defines the antonym of the phrase 'in kind'.
explanation.walkthrough: It looks like asking for a word opposite to "in kind"; instead IN plus VERSION gives a word meaning the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: turning something upside down or back to front produces its opposite.

clue.text: Non-specific leak in pipe (8)

indicators.note: 'in' places one piece within another, as water sits in a pipe

blocks.note: a wound or joint can weep

explanation.surface: A plumber vaguely reports a leak somewhere in the pipework.
explanation.walkthrough: "pipe" looks like plumbing, but it is the verb to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad generalisation that covers everything names nothing in particular.

clue.text: Lacking oxygen, nuts contain astringent (6)

indicators.note: 'nuts' means crazy, and crazy letters do not stay in their proper order

explanation.surface: Without oxygen, nuts hold a bitter substance.
explanation.walkthrough: "contain" looks like a container indicator; it is the fodder, with "nuts" as the anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Tannic wine or tea has a dry, astringent taste.
